gloss: old acquaintance; childhood friend; old friend

definitions.gloss: old acquaintance; childhood friend; old friend
definitions.explanation: A person one has known since long ago, typically from childhood or youth. Implies a deep, long-standing familiarity.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}とは{昔馴染|むかしなじ}みだ。
examples.english: He and I are old friends.

examples.japanese: {昔馴染|むかしなじ}みの{店|みせ}に{久|ひさ}しぶりに{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to a shop I've known for ages after a long time.

examples.japanese: {同窓会|どうそうかい}で{昔馴染|むかしなじ}みに{再会|さいかい}して、{懐|なつ}かしい{話|はなし}に{花|はな}が{咲|さ}いた。
examples.english: I reunited with old friends at a class reunion, and we blossomed into nostalgic conversation.

notes:
Composed of {昔|むかし} (the past, long ago) + {馴染|なじ}み (familiarity, acquaintance). Can refer to people, places, or shops that one has known for a long time.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {昔馴染|むかしなじ}みの{友人|ゆうじん}: an old friend from way back
- {昔馴染|むかしなじ}みの{店|みせ}: a shop one has frequented for years
- {昔馴染|むかしなじ}みに{再会|さいかい}する: to reunite with an old acquaintance

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {幼馴染|おさななじ}み: childhood friend — specifically someone known since early childhood; stronger implication of having grown up together
- {旧友|きゅうゆう}: old friend — more formal and literary
- {知|し}り{合|あ}い: acquaintance — neutral, without the nostalgic or long-standing nuance

USAGE:
Carries a warm, nostalgic tone. Unlike {幼馴染|おさななじ}み}, which specifically refers to childhood, {昔馴染|むかしなじ}み can refer to any long-standing connection from the past.
